## What is it?

A two-day datathon where teams will work together to analyse real-world infectious disease monitoring data. Participants will develop a full data science pipeline with prizes awarded for the best submission. 

## When is it?

-   **Friday 4 December**, 4pm--5pm: Online introductory session
<div style = "font-size: 0.8em; font-weight:100;">
_Recordings will be made available for people who can't make this session, although attendance is strongly encouraged_
</div>

- **Thursday 10th and Friday 11th December**, 9AM--5PM: Main event


## Who can participate?

* UNSW students interested in analysing health data.
* Enrol as a team of 5 or register individually to be placed on a team.

## Is it online or in-person?

The event will be in-person at the [UNSW Health Translation Hub](https://www.unsw.edu.au/precincts/rhip/hth).

## What skills do I need?

The approach to the datathon challenge is open ended---it could be a sophisticated predictive machine learning model or a simple data summary. At a minimum, you (or someone on your team) should be able to read in a dataset and do some basic data cleaning and summarisation using any software package of your choice. Effective teams combine members with different skill sets: epidemiological thinking is just as important as coding and algorithms. You also need someone on your team who can present and communicate your approach to the judging panel.

## The data

Participants will analyse deidentified real-world data on residential aged care quality from [Uniting](https://www.uniting.org), an Australian non-for-profit providing care and support through every life stage. Check out the [Data](/data.qmd) page for more information. 

## The datathon

### Pre-event: data release and online information session (Friday 4th December)

This is a chance to start interacting with your team, learn a bit more about the dataset and start thinking about potential analytic strategies.   

### The main event (Thursday 10th and Friday 11th December)

You will work with your team to develop and implement a data science pipeline to analyse Uniting's residential aged care quality data. There is no restriction on choice of software or analytic approach. At the end of the second day, each team will present their solution. Prizes will be awarded to the best submissions, evaluated by a panel of experts.

Lunch and morning tea and coffee will be provided. Dietary requirements can be noted in the registration form. 

## Registration

Visit the [registration page](registration.qmd) for details about registration.
